_comment: Editorial copy for the deck gallery. Art is composited into a three-card fan by cardz-win's scripts/build-deck-gallery.mjs — from the PNGs the app ships, or, for decks whose cards the app draws rather than loads, from cards the app renders itself (--export-decks). build.mjs refuses a slug with no art in assets/decks/manifest.json. 'credit' is optional and only present where art comes from outside the project.

decks.name: Felt House
decks.blurb: The house deck, and the one Cardz deals with until you choose otherwise. Classical proportions, a warm cream face, and a gold clubs medallion on the back.

decks.name: Valhalla
decks.blurb: A Norse woodcut deck. The courts are true two-headed figures, mirrored about the card's centre rather than merely drawn twice, and the pair of Loki jokers are worth finding.

decks.name: Scarab
decks.blurb: Ancient Egypt on papyrus. Alone among the decks it wears a small gold cartouche beside each index — the rank this card pairs with to make thirteen, which is Pyramid's whole problem solved in the corner of your eye.

decks.name: Olympus
decks.blurb: Gods painted on marble, with a gold index laid over the plate. A plain decorative deck: the corners hold the rank and the suit, nothing more.

decks.name: Herbarium
decks.blurb: A pressed-botanical plate book in ink and watercolour, with the four suits as four plant families — rose, marigold, clover, thistle — on a deep botanical-green table.

decks.name: Filigree
decks.blurb: Engraved vermilion and iron-gall ink, in the classic two-colour convention, laid on an antique espresso-leather writing desk.

decks.name: Ornamental
decks.blurb: The first illustrated deck Cardz shipped — vector ornament rasterized so that every hairline survives at card size, on a Victorian damask table.
decks.credit: Card art by Nicu Buculei, from his OpenClipart ornamental deck. Released into the public domain (CC0 1.0).

decks.name: Deepfield
decks.blurb: A space deck: dark navy cards, orbital pips, celestial courts, and four colours of suit instead of the usual two.

decks.name: Noir
decks.blurb: Neo-noir neon. Near-black cards in cyan and magenta, glowing two-headed courts, and a lit grid on the back.

decks.name: Monosolid
decks.blurb: Paper-cut shapes in two inks against a dark ink table. Type as image, tally pips, and courts cut down to a crown, an orb, and a blade.

note: Cardz also ships a Colourblind deck — blue hearts and diamonds against black spades and clubs — so that telling the suits apart never depends on telling red from green.
